portal_hypertension.abstract: The liver produces angiotensinogen (AGT), the key upstream precursor of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). We measured AGT levels in patients across distinct advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) stages and investigated the impact of AGT levels on clinical outcomes. We included clinically stable ACLD outpatients undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement between May 2018 and October 2023, as well as healthy controls (HCs) recruited in the prospective Vienna Cirrhosis Study (VICIS; NCT03267615). portal_hypertension.abstract: Since the first Baveno Consensus Conference in 1990, successive conferences held every 5 years have transformed the field of cirrhosis and portal hypertension, evolving from a focus on variceal bleeding to a pathophysiology-based framework centred on risk stratification, clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH), and the prevention of decompensation. Building on this progress, the Baveno Cooperation, in collaboration with the Vascular Liver Disease Interest Group (VALDIG), convened an expert faculty to review the evidence published since Baveno VII and update clinical guidance for patients with advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD), portal hypertension, and vascular liver diseases. portal_hypertension.abstract: The presence of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk esophageal varices (HREV) are major predictors of decompensation and mortality in chronic liver disease. Liver and spleen elastography are validated noninvasive markers of portal pressure, and increasing numbers of studies have integrated elastography measurements with conventional statistical and machine-learning (ML) models to predict these outcomes. This systematic review identified, critically appraised and synthesized studies developing or validating prediction models incorporating liver and/or spleen elastography for predicting CSPH and/or HREV. portal_hypertension.abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis after pLT. Our study analyzed data from the Portal vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers, across 18 countries, over a 20-year period.
